messages:
mira: heads-up — after the prefix cache landing on staging i'm seeing weirdly higher p95 for short-chat requests. baseline throughput actually dropped ~8% even though token usage decreased :confused:
jonathan: hmm, you mean the cached prefix reduces tokens but somehow batches are smaller and kernel throughput suffers?
sam_k: can you paste the profiler flame or p95 numbers? curious if it's a kernel-selection flip (short seq kernel vs long seq)
mira: attaching quick numbers: p50 28ms -> 26ms, p95 180ms -> 210ms. cache_hit_ratio went from 22% -> 72%. average decode tokens per request down 40%.
mira: hypothesis: packer targets token_budget=2048 and min_batch=4. with cached prefixes the "remaining_tokens" distribution collapses to small values, so continuous batcher forms many small micro-batches that pick the short-seq kernel more often and lose throughput on A100.
jonathan: that makes sense. short kernels have lower amortized kernel-launch overhead. but if we end up with a lot of small batches, we lose occupancy. also kernel selection table uses mean_seq_len threshold 64 which we're crossing more often now.
jonathan: quick profiler snippet (staging run):
```
# aggregated samples
kernel_short_launch_overhead: 32%
matmul_time_short: 18%
kv_lookup: 5%
queue_wait: 12%
```
mir a: (typo) mira: yep — queue_wait spikes around tail of load tests, esp when many cache-hit requests arrive concurrently. the packer currently ignores `cache_hit` metadata; it just cares about remaining_tokens.
sam_k: interesting — two angles: 1) make packer cache-hit aware (prefer grouping cache-hit requests together up to a different token budget), 2) bump token_budget when hit_ratio>threshold so batches can grow by waiting slightly longer.
jonathan: +1. maybe compute an effective_token = remaining_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_weight) or similar so hits don't collapse the budget so aggressively. we should tune cache_hit_weight in config.
perf-bot: CI perf check: staging run 1783456700 -> throughput -7.9%, p95 +16ms, avg cache_hit 71.3%
mira: prototype config i tried quickly:
```
packer:
  strategy: continuous
  target_token_budget: 2048
  min_batch_size: 4
  max_wait_ms: 30
  cache_hit_weight: 0.6  # scale remaining tokens for hit requests
  group_by_cache_hit: true
```
mira: with cache_hit_weight=0.6 p95 improved ~8ms and throughput recovered ~4%. group_by_cache_hit had mixed wins — reduced kernel flips but increased tail in some cases (more waiting).
jonathan: do we have a quick AB to test group_by_cache_hit toggled? also need to measure effect across different hardware (A100 vs T4) — kernel switching behavior differs.
sam_k: i'll spin two canaries: one with cache_hit_weight tuning, one with group_by_cache_hit on. capture p50/p95, throughput, kernel_flip_rate, queue_wait.
jonathan: add metric: `batcher.kernel_flip_rate` (count of batches where selected kernel != previous kernel on same worker) and `batcher.cache_hit_group_fraction`.
infra-bot: scheduled canary deployments: canary-1 (weight=0.6) -> started, canary-2 (group_by_cache_hit=true) -> started
mira: logging suggestion — include `remaining_tokens` histogram split by cache_hit=true/false so we can see distribution shift. also log per-batch `effective_token_budget` used.
sam_k: noted. i'll also dump a small flamegraph from A100 vs T4 after 15m run.
jonathan: action items: (1) collect histograms + kernel_flip_rate, (2) run canaries and compare, (3) if weight approach wins, roll to staging and adjust default packer configs, (4) consider packer prefetch hint to the runtime so kernels can pre-warm when a group of cache-hits finish quickly.
mira: thanks — i'll follow up with the staging dashboard link and a short writeup. :thumbsup:
jonathan: :eyes:
perf-bot: canary-1 (weight=0.6) results posted: p95 -5ms, throughput +3.9%
infra-bot: canary-2 (group_by_cache_hit) results posted: p95 -2ms, throughput +1.7%, queue_wait +4ms
mira: leaning toward weight-based scaling + a small max_wait bump. will prepare a PR to change defaults and add metrics.
sam_k: PR review when ready, i'll run heavier perf tests.
mira: ok closing this thread once PR is up. thanks everyone! :rocket:
